body:
Implements the third pillar of #574: a keyboard-driven quick-open for locating an element on a diagram by typing part of its label, type name, or other info.

**What it does**

- `Ctrl+G` opens a small, transient `JumpToElementDialog` over the current diagram — a `QLineEdit` above a live-filtered `QListWidget`.
- Typing filters the list against every element on the diagram, case-insensitively, matching against the element's instance label (`elementInformations().value("label")`), its type name (`Element::name()`), and every other `elementInformations()` value — so partial matches on any of those surface the element.
- `Up`/`Down` move through the filtered results (wrapping at either end), `Enter` selects the highlighted element on the diagram, calls `ensureVisible()` to scroll it into view, and closes the popup; `Escape` cancels without changing the current selection.
- The dialog is disposable — built fresh from `m_diagram->items()` each time it's opened, so it always reflects the diagram's current state with no persistent list to keep in sync.

**Design notes**

- Candidates are built once on open (`buildCandidates()`) rather than re-scanning `items()` on every keystroke, so filtering a live-typed query stays cheap even on larger diagrams.
- `QPointer<Element>` guards each candidate against the (unlikely but possible) case of an element being deleted out from under the dialog while it's open; `activateCurrentItem()` and `updateFilteredList()` both check it before dereferencing.
- Reuses `QDialog`'s standard `eventFilter()` override on the line edit rather than subclassing `QLineEdit`, keeping the arrow/enter/escape handling colocated with the rest of the dialog's logic in one file.

**Testing**

Beyond compiling clean (full CMake build, zero new warnings), verified end-to-end in a real running session (Xvfb + xdotool) against a multi-transistor schematic:
- `Ctrl+G` opens the popup with the full element list and focus on the text field.
- Typing live-filters the list correctly against label, type name, and element info fields.
- `Up`/`Down` move the highlighted row and wrap at both ends.
- `Enter` selects the correct element on the diagram, scrolls it into view, and closes the popup.
- `Escape` closes the popup without altering the diagram's prior selection.

*Developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).*

commits.messageBody:
Implements the third pillar of #574: a lightweight quick-open popup
for jumping straight to an element on the current diagram, rather
than scrolling/scanning visually.

New JumpToElementDialog (sources/ui/): a small QDialog with a filter
QLineEdit and a live-filtered QListWidget beneath it. Built from
every Element on the diagram, searchable against its label
(elementInformations().value("label")), type name (Element::name()),
and every other element information value, joined into one
lowercased search string per candidate. Up/Down move through the
filtered list, Enter selects the highlighted element on the diagram
(clearing the rest of the selection) and scrolls it into view via
ensureVisible(), Escape cancels without changing the current
selection. All three are handled via an event filter on the line
edit, so the user never has to leave the text field to navigate or
confirm.

Triggered by a new Ctrl+G action in QETDiagramEditor, added next to
the existing Ctrl+F "search and replace" action and to the Edit
menu. Confirmed free: not used anywhere in qetdiagrameditor.cpp or
qetmainwindow.cpp today.

Explicitly not a duplicate of the existing SearchAndReplace module
(also on this menu, via Ctrl+F): that's a bulk property search/replace
tool across whole diagrams; this is a single-item navigational
popup with no editing capability.

Verified end-to-end in a real running session (Xvfb + xdotool)
against a multi-transistor schematic: Ctrl+G opens the popup listing
every element; typing "Q16" live-filters down to the one match;
arrow keys move the highlighted row through the filtered list;
Enter selects the highlighted element (confirmed via the properties
panel showing its label) and closes the popup; Escape closes it
without changing the selection.

See discussion #574.
